body:
My guess is that we're now doing an extra render pass, maybe to bake the area lights, that changed the order in which things happen.

@CookieBadger anything you can think of that your PR introduces that could explain why we're seeing this behaviour? I realise you're probably not up to speed to how the override system works in XR but basically on the main viewport, we don't use Godots render targets but override them with an OpenXR supplied one. This however happens just before the viewport is rendered.

Ok, I dove a little deeper into this. I think we've just been lucky in the past because the order hasn't changed. It might just be that we set some info a little earlier, might even be related to the viewport PR I did and we may be wrong about it  being related to the area lights PR.

`pre_render` was always called first, then we call `pre_draw_viewport` for each XR marked viewport, and we update our swapchains in `pre_draw_viewport`. Probably in the past we didn't have certain info set that resulted in the logic in `on_pre_render` to be skipped. Now with the viewport changes we do have this info.

It's important to note that this is historic, `pre_render` was introduced much much later and I think we could safely move the swapchain update/create logic from `pre_draw_viewport` into `pre_render` so it's executed before we call `on_pre_render` on each extension.

Alright, it looks like the change in order was actually caused by PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116220 (so, my fault :-)) and when testing with space warp, it will actually crash with Godot 4.7-dev3 (and work fine with Godot 4.7-dev2)

The weird thing is that when testing with frame synthesis (which is what I was testing while bisecting), it doesn't start crashing until Godot 4.7-dev5, specifically, after PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/108219. Something allowed us to get lucky with frame synthesis until that other PR tipped us over the edge

So, now it's a question of: does PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116220 really need the change in order, or is there another way to accomplish what it needs to do? Or, if it does need the change in order, are we OK a compatibility break here?

I'll keep digging into this :-)

Soo... yeah, I don't really have much insight into XR and render targets. As for #108219, it adds a number of things, that could cause some needs for adjustment. What it does add:
- two lookup table textures that are being sampled (per render pipeline)
- a sampler for the area light atlas with mipmaps
- a cluster buffer for area lights
- a shader directive #AREA_LIGHT_CODE_USED
- order of uniform bindings has also been modified

In terms of render passes, the only thing that comes to mind is the generation of the area light atlas mipmaps which uses a copy-effect to progressively blur the layers, i.e. a compute shader. Let me know if you need some specific info.
@CookieBadger It's really not the fault of your changes. It's my change that caused the underlying issue, but somehow the crash just wasn't being triggered until your change

> So, now it's a question of: does PR [#116220](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116220) really need the change in order, or is there another way to accomplish what it needs to do? Or, if it does need the change in order, are we OK a compatibility break here?

It does look like PR #116220 needs to move the swapchain creation to `on_pre_draw_viewport(RID p_render_target)` because that one actually gets the `RID` of the render target, and it needs to have that in order to decide if subsampled images can be enabled or not

And, if we are switching subsampled images from enabled to disabled (or vice-versa) then the swapchains need to be recreated, because we need to create them with the subsampled flag or not

The best option I could think of to attempt to restore compatibility was to (re-)create the swapchains in both places (`on_pre_render()` and `on_pre_draw_viewport()`), but it isn't ideal.

The main downside is that when OpenXR first starts up, if subsampled images are enabled and supported, it would create the main swapchains, and then, just a little while later (before anything has even been rendered), destroy them and create them again with the subsampled flag.

Also, I tried this, and it worked for space warp in the godot_openxr_vendors extension, but it didn't fix frame synthesis because that one also isn't expecting the main swapchains to get recreated twice in a row, and it still crashes. Of course, we could modify it's code and fix that, but this means it doesn't fully restore compatibility.

Does anyone have any other ideas to restore compatibility?

My inclination at the moment is to decide to keep the compatibility breakage from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116220, document it in the 4.6 -> 4.7 upgrading docs, and merge the changes for space warp and frame synthesis.

Looking at both life-cycles (the 4.6 and earlier vs 4.7), I think the current 4.7 one makes the most sense: we now have a hook that runs before they are created (`on_pre_render()`) which could be useful, we only create them when there is actually a viewport with `use_xr = true`, and we have access to the render target when creating the swapchains

I also suspect there are very few extensions that actually depend on the old order - it may _only_ be space warp and frame synthesis? I looked through the others in Godot and godot_openxr_vendors, and there aren't any others that seem like they'd be affected

@BastiaanOlij @m4gr3d @devloglogan What do you guys think?
